newsitem.title: CHINA: Shanghai copper ends down on speculative selling.
newsitem.headline: Shanghai copper ends down on speculative selling.

text.p: Shanghai copper futures ended down across the board on Wednesday on speculative selling by retail investors, traders said.
The most actively traded August 1997 contract ended at 23,360 yuan ($2,816) per tonne, losing 140 yuan. It opened at an intraday high of 23,460 and a low of 23,270 yuan.
May fell 100 yuan to 23,300, June 120 to 23,380, July 150 to 23,350, September 130 to 23,350 and October 110 to 23,290.
Combined volume rose to 30,460 tonnes from 9,610 tonnes.
Copper opened slightly lower with most contracts at their intraday highs. It moved to low levels for most of the session.
"Retail investors dominated today's trading with most of them disappointed about the recent performance of the LME (London Metal Exchange)," one trader said.
"Some investors liquidated their long positions today in order to avoid short-term risks," he said.
LME copper has been consolidating below $2,400 a tonne for the past couple of weeks. In early Wednesday trading, it was seen moving lower after LME copper stocks rose by 3,050 tonnes.
Shanghai traders said firm physical copper prices in the Shanghai area, now around 23,400 yuan per tonne, would prevent copper from falling sharply.
"Technical charts also do not support sharp falls in futures prices in the short term but Shanghai copper needs positive news to boost investors' confidence," a second trader said.
Traders said they expected the LME to provide some clear signs to Shanghai copper in the short term.
Aluminium ended down. May fell 30 yuan to 15,270, June 30 to 15,550 and July 100 to 15,600.
Combined volume rose to 800 tonnes from 180 tonnes.
